extracted.intended_audience: fans of stand-up comedy and aspiring one-liner comedians; general readers interested in comedic technique
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for crafting and performing concise, self-contained one-line jokes that rely on literal pivots, visual imagery, delivery, and economy of language. Emphasizes how tiny language, timing, and attitude create durable comedic effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-liner engineering and effortless appearance
rubrics_metrics.description: He walked on stage, squinted into the lights, and dropped perfectly engineered one-liners like they were casual observations he’d just discovered backstage. It felt effortless. It wasn’t.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make jokes that read as casual observations but are tightly constructed—precision of wording and economy of setup make the line appear effortless even though it’s engineered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical correctness is undefeated
rubrics_metrics.description: "I haven’t slept for ten days…because that would be too long." — a simple twist using literal accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use literal/technical correctness to pivot audience expectations (expect one meaning, deliver a literally accurate alternative). The 'tiny pivot' differentiates the joke.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hedberg effect: single-line cognitive reframe
rubrics_metrics.description: “An escalator can never break. It can only become stairs.” — one sentence that permanently adjusts how you perceive an object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for a single sentence that reorients perception; a one-liner that makes the audience think differently about an everyday thing long after the joke is done.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual, absurd, and relatable imagery
rubrics_metrics.description: "Rice is great if you’re really hungry and want to eat two thousand of something." — visual, absurd, and completely relatable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine a clear visual image with an absurd element that remains relatable; brevity plus concrete imagery strengthens the punchline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Escalation without vocal escalation
rubrics_metrics.description: "I think Bigfoot is blurry...There’s a large, out-of-focus monster roaming the countryside." — escalation that doesn't raise his voice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build escalation through the idea and imagery rather than through louder delivery; a calm delivery that increases absurdity can be very effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Premise contradiction / self-defeating premise
rubrics_metrics.description: "I’m against picketers, but I don’t know how to show it." — the premise defeats itself instantly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use contradictions where the joke's setup undermines its own logic; the humor lives in the internal inconsistency of the premise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seemingly ridiculous idea that becomes internally reasonable
rubrics_metrics.description: "I like refried beans. That’s why I wanna try fried beans. Because maybe they’re just as good, and we’re wasting time."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present an absurd or ridiculous notion, then let the joke reveal a quirky internal logic that makes the audience briefly accept it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literal/definitional twists
rubrics_metrics.description: "Every book is a children’s book if the kid can read." — technically flawless, slightly chaotic, completely airtight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exploit literal definitions or semantic loopholes to twist a familiar category or saying into an unexpected conclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimal setup and speed
rubrics_metrics.description: "I saw a wino eating grapes. I was like, ‘Dude, you have to wait.’" — fast, visual, no explanation needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep setups extremely short; a rapid economy of words that yields an immediate image often lands faster and cleaner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subverting clichés and motivational phrases
rubrics_metrics.description: "I’m sick of following my dreams. I’m just going to ask them where they’re going and hook up with them later."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take well-worn motivational language and reframe it in a mundane or self-interested way to undercut sincerity and generate humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elevating mundane behavior into philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: "My fake plants died because I did not pretend to water them." — laziness elevated to philosophy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Turn ordinary, even lazy, actions into grand or philosophical observations to create comedic contrast.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small linguistic changes yield big consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: "I wrote a letter to my dad. I said, ‘I really enjoy being here.’ But I accidentally wrote ‘rarely.’" — a typo with emotional consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage tiny language shifts (one letter, one word) to create a surprising reinterpretation or emotional punch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Name/wordplay-based identity humor
rubrics_metrics.description: "I wish my name was Brian, because maybe sometimes people would misspell it ‘Brain.’"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use names, homophones, or spelling to create self-deprecating or identity-based wordplay that feels intimate and clever.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delivery as material (mumbling/deadpan)
rubrics_metrics.description: "I’m a mumbler... if I mumble, I might as well be talking to you in Morse code." — he turned delivery into material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make your vocal style (mumble, deadpan, cadence) part of the joke itself; delivery and content should reinforce each other.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reframing by unexpected attribute
rubrics_metrics.description: "I like to play blackjack. I’m not addicted to gambling. I’m addicted to sitting in a semi-circle." — not about risk, about geometry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinterpret an activity by highlighting an unrelated attribute (geometry, logistics) to create a fresh perspective and surprise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creating indelible visuals you can't unsee
rubrics_metrics.description: "Dogs are forever in the push-up position." — you can’t unsee it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft one-line images so vivid and precise that they permanently change how the audience views something ordinary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blunt logical absurdism
rubrics_metrics.description: "If you’re flammable and have legs, you are never blocking a fire exit." — pure blunt logic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State a logical-sounding rule that leads to an absurd conclusion; the delivery of blunt 'reason' sells the joke.

rubrics_metrics.name: Turning minor inconveniences into philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: "I bought a doughnut, and they gave me a receipt for the doughnut... We don’t need to bring ink and paper into this." — a minor inconvenience becomes philosophy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exaggerate and philosophize small, everyday annoyances to reveal their absurdity and create comic weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Playing with scale and perspective
rubrics_metrics.description: "Baked potatoes are like regular potatoes, but to me, they’re huge." — scale becomes comedy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use comparative scale or subjective perspective to make a mundane item feel unexpectedly outsized or tiny for comedic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using unnecessary/detail to produce surprise
rubrics_metrics.description: "I don’t wear a watch because I want my arms to weigh the same." and "I’m not afraid of a spider, but I’m afraid of a spider that’s wearing a hat."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add an unnecessary or bizarre detail (weight balance, spider hat) to a normal statement to create a surprising and memorable twist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Backward/inverse logic that makes sense
rubrics_metrics.description: "I bought a seven-dollar pen because I always lose pens, and I got sick of not caring." — backward logic that makes sense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reverse or sunk-cost style reasoning in a way that initially sounds irrational but reveals a peculiar internal logic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-word flips or one-word pivots
rubrics_metrics.description: "I tried to walk into Target, but I missed." — one word flips everything.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely on a single-word misdirection or pivot that reinterprets the setup; economy makes a one-word flip land sharply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Juxtaposing lofty ideas with mundane logistics
rubrics_metrics.description: "I want to hang a map of the world... But first, I’m gonna have to travel to the top two corners of the map so it won’t fall down."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start with an inspirational or grand idea and undercut it with a practical, prosaic problem to produce surprise and comedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Puns delivered as accidental discoveries
rubrics_metrics.description: "They gave me another one, free of charge." — it’s a pun. But delivered like an accidental discovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use wordplay and puns but present them deadpan or as if they were obvious observations to keep them fresh rather than groan-worthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete, self-contained joke/universe
rubrics_metrics.description: He made every joke feel like a tiny, self-contained universe. He perfected them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for jokes that require no external callbacks to land—compact setups and punchlines that form a full idea in one line.
